title: Phased Compatibility Contract & Migration Pipeline for Legacy Multi‑Endpoint Transport
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines the contract, migration pipeline, acceptance criteria, and communications for removing the legacy multi-endpoint transport surface (legacy-jsonrpc, multipoll, and bulk-embed sync endpoints) and migrating customers to the unified /inference API. The intent is a data-safe, low-friction transition that preserves telemetry and billing continuity while providing clear rollback and outage safety nets.
goals: 1) Provide a deterministic phased decommission timeline with contractual exposure windows for customers. 2) Deliver a migration pipeline (shadowing, opt-in parity, SDK adapter, telemetry/quality gates) that prevents >2% regression in production L7 errors or quality metrics. 3) Ensure billing continuity and clear chargeback guidance for customers during the transition.
success_metrics: - <2% increase in 5xx error rate across migrated customers during each phase. - <1% increase in token cost for customers who adopt default migration guidance. - 90% of active legacy callers either migrated or enrolled in a shadow run within the exposure window. - Zero P0 incidents attributable to unhandled transport differences during rollout.
scope: IN SCOPE: Contracted exposure windows (90/180/365 day tiers), automated SDK adapter for common languages, opt-in shadowing mode in Console, telemetry gating (quality and latency), per-customer migration dashboards, billing reconciliation tooling. OUT OF SCOPE: Forced immediate cutoffs for unresponsive enterprise customers, major protocol changes to unified API beyond what existing clients can emulate, rearchitecting model alias semantics (handled under separate initiative).
non_goals: We will not build a permanent long-term compat shim that maintains legacy protocol indefinitely. We will not automatically rewrite client traffic at the edge without explicit customer consent. We will not migrate customers' data stores or non-Redwood third-party bridges as part of this ticket.
requirements: Define a three-tier exposure contract (Short: 90 days, Standard: 180 days, Extended: 365 days) and criteria to qualify for extended tier (enterprise SLA + signed addendum).

Provide an SDK adapter package (Node, Python, Java) that translates legacy transports into /inference calls, implements streaming semantics, and optionally rewrites model aliases to pinned stable versions.
Implement Console-UI and API endpoints for: migration enrollment, shadow mode toggle, migration status per-customer, and billing reconciliation reports.
Telemetry: Emit per-request migration tags, latency histograms, token delta, and quality regression markers tied to canonical prompt sets (prompt-sets managed in Optimize).

Create a rollback/circuit breaker policy: automatic throttling if 5xx >2% or quality regression >3% on canonical prompts, with automatic reversion to legacy transport for impacted customers until remediation.
Legal and Billing: Contract addendum templates, invoice line item mapping for 'compat adapter' usage during the exposure window, and customer notification templates per exposure tier.
Acceptance tests: Integration tests for streaming fidelity (SSE/Chunk vs. WebSocket), ordering guarantees for multiplexed requests, and end-to-end latency tests under representative batch sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Migration contract documents signed or published and available to self-serve customers in Console for all three tiers.
SDK adapter packages published to npm/pypi/maven with release notes and a migration guide; automated integration examples exist in the repo and pass CI.
Shadow mode: at least one Canary customer group enrolled and shadowing traffic with metrics visible in Console; no regressions beyond thresholds after 14 days.
Telemetry: Migration-specific metrics are surfaced in Console runbooks and SLO dashboards; alerts configured for the circuit breaker thresholds.
Billing: Generated reconciliation report for adapter usage that matches billing system sample invoices within 1% delta for two pilot customers.
Runbook: On-call playbook created with clear steps to rollback, notify customers, and escalate to Eng/PM/Legal.
rollout_phases: Phase 0 - Prep (2 weeks): legal templates, Console UX mocks, SDK skeletons. Internal dry-run with test tenants.
Phase 1 - Pilots (4 weeks): onboard 3 pilot customers across tiers into shadow mode. Validate telemetry gates and billing mapping. Iterate SDK.
Phase 2 - Early Access (8 weeks): open enrollment for self-serve customers, publish migration guide, and provide onboarding office hours.
Phase 3 - Gradual Enforcement (90-day short tier begins): begin auto-routing new customers away from legacy transports; existing customers continue within exposure windows.
Phase 4 - Tiered Decommission (90/180/365): at each tier expiration, attempt automated migration; if customer non-responsive escalate to account team and follow contract.
telemetry_gates: Canonical prompt-sets will be used to surface quality regressions. Gate conditions: block progression if 5xx >2% sustained over 1 hour OR quality drop (per-example BLEU/ROUGE surrogate or embedding-similarity delta) >3% across canonical prompts. Console alerts will create a rollback action that can automatically route affected traffic back to legacy transport while a hotfix is deployed.
comms_plan: - T-minus 60-day announcement email to all owners of tenants using legacy transports with clear exposure tier and migration resources. - Weekly migration status digest for accounts in Early Access. - Office hours and webinar series for self-serve SDK onboarding. - Dedicated channel for enterprise accounts with Partner/AM outreach. - Public deprecation notice in API docs and changelog 30 days before Short-tier enforcement.
developer_tasks: ENG-8421: Implement server-side migration tag and routing flags.
ENG-9102: Build SDK adapter for Node/Python/Java with streaming parity tests.
ENG-9203: Console UI for migration enrollment and per-tenant status.
ENG-9317: Telemetry pipeline updates to capture canonical prompt performance and migration flags.
sdk_changes: Adapter will expose a shim API that matches legacy method signatures and supports optional parameter mapping. Default behavior should preserve streaming semantics; where exact parity is impossible we require an explicit opt-in flag with visible warning. SDKs must include migration examples and a compatibility test harness to run the customer’s saved prompt-sets against both transports.
dependencies_details: Legal needs to finalize the exposure contract templates. Billing needs to support temporary invoice line items and reconciliation exports. Security must re-review SDK packaging for new dependencies and signing. Eng teams owning routing and runtime must implement circuit breakers and fallback routing APIs.

2026-04-12: First pilot completes shadow validation; telemetry gates exercised.
2026-05-01: Early Access opens; migration guides published.
2026-06-30: Target date for first enforcement (Short - 90 day) to begin rolling phase-outs for new non-enrolled customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Undetected quality regressions affecting customer experience. Mitigation: Require canonical prompt-sets and conservative gating with manual review for flagged regressions.
Risk: Billing disputes during exposure window. Mitigation: Provide reconciliation reports and offer a 30-day dispute window with temporary credits as needed.
Risk: Enterprise customers require longer support. Mitigation: Offer extended tier via signed addendum and prioritized migration support from Solutions Eng.
Risk: SDK adapter introduces security vulnerabilities. Mitigation: Security review and signed artifacts; limit dependencies and require SCA scanning in CI.
notes: This ticket emphasizes a contractual, phased approach instead of a blunt cutover. The intention is to use the adapter and shadowing approach to empirically validate parity before client switchover. Feedback from the pilot customers will feed into the migration guide and default flags. Coordinate with PM-523410 for client-specific playbooks.
